entities.summary:
Jan (Jean) I Carondelet (born unknown, died 1502-03-12) was a Burgundian jurist and politician who played a significant role in the governance of the Burgundian Netherlands during the late Middle Ages.

As the son of Jean Carondelet and Jeanne de Basan, Jan inherited a prominent position in the Burgundian court and demonstrated exceptional legal acumen, earning him a reputation as a skilled jurist.

Jan's most notable achievement was his involvement in the negotiations leading to the Treaty of Cambrai in 1502, a landmark agreement that marked a significant turning point in the relations between the Burgundian Netherlands and the French monarchy.

Jan's legacy extends beyond his political accomplishments, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Catholic Church.

"A man of great learning and piety, Jan Carondelet was a true embodiment of the Burgundian ideal of nobility."
